# Our first session

Start the native demo in one terminal (build it first as shown in
[Building the target](../native_journey/building_the_target.qmd)):

```bash
$ ./native_demo
Native Demo -- license gate
Find the key, or patch the gate
attempts: 1
Enter license key (q to quit):
```

In another terminal, first confirm that the host ptrace prerequisite is
enabled:

```bash
$ cat /proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope
0
```

If it prints `1`, run `sudo sysctl -w kernel.yama.ptrace_scope=0` as shown in
[Setting up the lab](setting_up_the_lab.qmd), then find the pid in the same
shell. `Frpj` also lists local processes:

```bash
$ rizin -N -q -c 'Frpj' malloc://512
{"ok":true,"result":{"processes":[{"pid":1,"name":"init"},...]}}
```

Or ask the system from the shell:

```bash
$ pgrep -x native_demo
46117
```

## Open the session

```text
[0x00000000]> Froj frida://attach/local//46117
{"ok":true,"result":{"action":"attach","pid":46117,"resumed":false,"state":"attached"}}
```

![Attaching locally](img/first_steps/attach-local.png)

We are attached. The demo is still running and waiting for input: attaching
does not stop it.

> **Note:** pids change every run. Read yours from `pgrep` or `Frpj`.

Attach by name works too: the pid is resolved at attach time:

```text
[0x00000000]> Frcj
{"ok":true,"result":{"pid":46117,"state":"closed"}}

[0x00000000]> Froj frida://attach/local//native_demo
{"ok":true,"result":{"action":"attach","pid":46117,"resumed":false,"state":"attached"}}
```

## Ping the agent

`Frij` loads the agent into the target on first use and asks for its
identity:

```text
[0x00000000]> Frij
{"ok":true,"result":{"version":1,"platform":"linux","arch":"x64","pointerSize":8}}
```

- `version` is the agent protocol version (1)
- `platform` is the target's platform
- `arch` is the target architecture
- `pointerSize` is 8 on 64-bit targets

This is the quickest way to confirm the host-agent channel is alive.

## What the session state says

```text
[0x00000000]> Frsj
{"ok":true,"result":{"active":true,"state":"attached","pid":46117,"action":"attach","target":"46117"}}
```

`Frsj` reports `active`, `state`, `pid`, `action` and `target`. Without a
session it reports:

```text
{"ok":true,"result":{"active":false,"state":"closed"}}
```

## Close

```text
[0x00000000]> Frcj
{"ok":true,"result":{"pid":46117,"state":"closed"}}
```

The demo keeps running: attached targets are not killed on close.

## The whole session as a chained command

```bash
$ rizin -N -q \
    -c 'Froj frida://attach/local//native_demo' \
    -c 'Frij' \
    -c 'Frcj' malloc://512
{"ok":true,"result":{"action":"attach","pid":46117,"resumed":false,"state":"attached"}}
{"ok":true,"result":{"version":1,"platform":"linux","arch":"x64","pointerSize":8}}
{"ok":true,"result":{"pid":46117,"state":"closed"}}
```

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
    participant R as rizin
    participant F as frida-core
    participant T as native_demo
    R->>F: attach local pid
    F-->>R: attached
    R->>F: ping (Frij)
    F->>T: inject agent
    T-->>F: agent.ready
    F->>T: ping request
    T-->>F: version, platform, arch, pointerSize
    F-->>R: {version:1, ...}
    R->>F: detach (Frcj)
    F-->>R: closed
```

::: {.callout-tip}
### Try

Open a session on `native_demo`, ping the agent, read `Frsj`, then close.
Watch the demo keep running in its terminal.
:::
